digest.component_or_area: tickets-store reconciler cache and history optimization
propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB, with 92% being the reconciler's .bridge_state cache; only 55 MB is actual ticket event data.

Diffing consecutive committed bindings.json revisions shows zero changes to baseline value but 1144 changes to baseline_advanced_at (unused timestamp) and 20 rotation bookkeeping changes per pass, causing scattered edits that defeat git delta compression.

Measured marginal cost per version is 12.79 KB today; deleting the timestamp reduces it to 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement) and moving rotation bookkeeping reduces it 12.8x total, with git repack achieving 8.4% of original size.
The .bridge_state cache must remain committed on-branch because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners, making durable state dependent on git.
A one-time history strip using git fast-export/filter/fast-import reduces 1.17 GiB to 98.8 MB while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges, with HEAD tree byte-identical after dynamic re-add.

Rollout gates for A2-2 and reclaim are gated by descendant workflow execution, explicit host refresh, mixed-version self-healing, and live epoch-refusal probes from deployed runtimes, with no fixed-delay requirements.
